summary: Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling withholds skin-aging credit and makes knee pain an optional future qualification. The four existing signed contexts (all non-eligible) already match: 37432180 (26 RCTs, co-actives present), 40324552 (benefit absent in non-pharma-funded and high-quality subgroups), 37717022 (4 high-risk-of-bias knee trials), 39839727 (collagen-plus-calcium-ascorbate formula). Only the 40324552 included-study list is outstanding.

record_updates.notes: Signed A059/A148 review rejects affirmative generic-product qualification from these four sources without eligible preparation/dose/population/outcome correspondence. Favorable pooled skin measurements are retained with co-active, quality and funding limitations; OA pooling has an unresolved active-comparator/repeated-outcome problem; COLLinstant is a collagen-plus-calcium-ascorbate formula, not monotherapy. This is a scoped eligibility hold, not a penalty or a claim that all collagen is ineffective. Source-specific reviewed limitations are recorded separately from unresolved applicability/full-text questions. Dr.Pham signed the returned decisions; approval date2026-10-26 supplied by the operator. Dr. Pham's signed ruling of 2026-10-28 resolves the former record-level eligibility hold: skin-aging credit is withheld (completed no-credit, reference path). Knee-osteoarthritis pain credit is an optional future qualification requiring exact-source acceptance and does not block this completion.

limitations: The signed return rejects unqualified generic-product efficacy; a source-specific favorable finding does not establish equivalence of retail preparations.
No transfer to BioCell, UC-II, cartilage regeneration, exercise recovery or longevity, and no universal collagen efficacy dose.
Original saved-label preparation, component dose, regimen and outcome correspondence remain separately required.
Favorable pooled measurements do not establish visible rejuvenation or every product. Missing-data, deviations and reporting-bias concerns remain.

The Methods say combination supplements were excluded, but included Table1 references include astaxanthin, vitamins, coenzymeQ10, ornithine or other active formulations; isolated-collagen attribution is not established.
Some included references have no verified PMID; no identifier is invented. Review reports hospital funding and no conflicts, which does not establish independence of its underlying trials.

The later funding/quality-sensitive review and DOI10.1111/jocd.71208 methodological challenge must not be omitted; that critique is not a formal retraction and its reanalysis is not independently reproduced here.

Table1 identifies Trc2011 control as1.5g/day glucosamine sulfate, not placebo, despite the review labeling its pooled contrast placebo-controlled.
